title: Bursa’s Ottoman civic centres expand
summary: Early Ottoman Bursa grew around complexes combining mosques, schools, baths and public kitchens. Endowed institutions linked urban neighbourhoods with rural communities such as nearby Cumalıkızık.

claims.text: Early Ottoman Bursa grew around complexes combining mosques, schools, baths and public kitchens. Endowed institutions linked urban neighbourhoods with rural communities such as nearby Cumalıkızık.
Early fourteenth to mid-fifteenth-century development, following the source’s planning history.

Urban life emerges here through services and economic relationships as well as royal rule. The documented connection between city institutions and rural support distinguishes this example from a purely monumental account.
